analysis.subject: finance
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains compound interest with a $100 example at 5% interest each year through $105 and $110.25, projects growth to more than $162 in 10 years and almost $340 in 25 years, teaches the Rule of 72 with 72 divided by 9 equals 8, and includes pizza savings activities with $730 growing to $931.69 in five years and $3,155.02 in 30 years.

overview.headline: How compound interest earns interest on interest over time

keyPoints.point: Compound interest means you earn interest on interest already earned from the deposit.
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is the interest you earn on interest.

keyPoints.point: A $100 deposit that earns 5% interest each year grows to $105 at the end of the first year.
keyPoints.quote: if you have $100 and it earns 5% interest each year, you'll have $105 at the end of the first year.

keyPoints.point: In the second year the balance reaches $110.25 because you also earn interest on the earlier $5 of interest.
keyPoints.quote: At the end of the second year, you'll have $110.25.

keyPoints.point: The Rule of 72 estimates doubling time when you divide 72 by the expected rate of return.
keyPoints.quote: Simply divide the number 72 by your investment’s expected rate of return (interest rate).

keyTerms.gloss: interest that is earned on interest already added to the account
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is the interest you earn on interest.

keyTerms.gloss: expected rate of return used to estimate investment growth
keyTerms.quote: Simply divide the number 72 by your investment’s expected rate of return (interest rate).

keyTerms.gloss: way to estimate how long an investment will take to double
keyTerms.quote: The Rule of 72 is a great way to estimate how your investment will grow over time.

keyTerms.gloss: money placed to earn a return and grow over time
keyTerms.quote: Assuming an expected rate of return of 9%, your investment will double in value about every 8 years (72 divided by 9 equals 8).
